content.text:
**Finding submitted: compliant** (no redline).

**What I checked and why:**

| Area | Paragraphs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fees / payment terms | p0050–p0070 | Purely usage-based volume tiers; no minimum commitment or shortfall true-up |
| Term & termination rights | p0049, p0132–p0137 | On Licensor termination for breach, Licensor retains only "the right to receive payments for all trades performed" — accrued fees, not remaining contract value |
| Effect of termination | p0138 | Cease use, return materials, officer certificate — no exit payment |
| Remedies / termination damages | p0142 | Mutual bar on termination damages — runs in our favour |
| Supplemental Payments & tier table | p0074, p0078–p0083 | Share of amounts actually received from third parties; no stipulated damages |
| General provisions | p0144–p0160 | No penalty or late-payment interest; attorneys' fees provision is mutual |

Full-text searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "minimum" and "interest" returned nothing relevant — the first two returned zero hits entirely.

**Conclusion:** the rule's *preferred* position is satisfied by absence, so no early-termination-fee cap fallback is needed.

Two items I deliberately did **not** flag:
- **Audit cost-shifting on a >5% discrepancy (p0064)** — conditional reimbursement of actual audit cost, not stipulated damages. Worth noting commercially (it is uncapped and triggered by any 5% variance), but it belongs to an audit/records rule, not LD.
- **Bonus and rebate shares (p0075–p0076)** — these run from Licensor to us, i.e. value in our favour, expressly compliant under the detection guidance.

One drafting oddity flagged for awareness rather than redline under this rule: p0070 states "In no event shall the amount payable by the **Licensor** be less than…" in a clause that otherwise governs *Licensee's* fee calculation. This reads as a scrivener's error for "Licensee". It is a floor tied to recorded trade volume rather than a liquidated sum, so it does not fail the LD fallback — but if it is meant to say "Licensee", it deserves attention under the fees/payment rule.
